name: Charcoal Drawing / Pastel
visualIdentity: Supplemental reference, not a directly named source-collection style. Charcoal uses tonal mass, hatching and smudging; pastel uses softly layered pigment and visible grain. Preserve paper texture and localized powder edges as marks reveal or erase. Avoid uniform noise that obscures structure. Charcoal and pastel are distinct techniques; choose one as primary.
suitableUses: Explicit good fits include product and editorial introductions, explanatory or illustrated narratives, abstract or cinematic sequences, and documentary or moody storytelling. Chaptered motion suits material with meaningful stages. Rotoscoped figure motion suits dance, sports or documentary vignettes when footage is supplied. These are inferred fit, not guarantees.
limitations: A chapter transition may be unnecessary for a short topic, obscure causality, introduce an unexplained change, or break a continuous shot or loop. Avoid added colors, uniform noise, moving paper texture, photo detail retention, and unsupported footage. No intrinsic pastel palette or fixed soundtrack is specified. Supplemental status limits claims about canonical source styling.
palette: The example is reference-dependent, not canonical: opaque background #EDE7DC and foreground #353330, a monochrome two-color pair with no gradient. Task exact colors, approved brand/reference palettes, semantic mappings and asset colors take precedence. Preserve roles and color families; use hatching, patterns or opacity for tone, not extra accent hues. motionAndInteraction: Build separate charcoal-value or pastel-color layers with fixed-grain brushes and smudge masks; reveal or erase marks locally. Use restrained movement and preserve paper-anchored grain. Optional chapter handoffs coordinate outgoing/incoming scenes and copy on shared progress; storytelling can map finite scroll to ordered states and reading holds. combinations: Works best alone for tonal drawings. Optional style-101 atmospheric depth uses limited tonal planes and slow drift or local reveals; keep grain anchored to paper and movement limited, with no added colors. These are suggestions, not required pairings.
